   121	/-- Natural powers of a generalized Pauli observable multiply its label by
   122	repeated addition. -/
   123	private theorem primeTauObservable_pow_nat {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   124	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
   125	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (n : ℕ) :
   126	    (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n =
   127	      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) := by
   128	  induction n with
   129	  | zero =>
   130	      rw [pow_zero]
   131	      have hzero : (fun i => (0 : ℕ) • a i) = (0 : ι → K) := by
   132	        funext i
   133	        simp
   134	      rw [hzero]
   135	      exact (primeTauObservable_zero (p := p) (K := K) (ι := ι) W).symm
   136	  | succ n ih =>
   137	      calc
   138	        (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ (n + 1) =
   139	            (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n *
   140	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := pow_succ _ _
   141	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) *
   142	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := by rw [ih]
   143	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W ((fun i => n • a i) + a) :=
   144	              primeTauObservable_mul W _ _
   145	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
   146	              have hlabels : ((fun i => n • a i) + a) =
   147	                  (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
   148	                funext i
   149	                rw [Pi.add_apply, add_nsmul, one_nsmul]
   150	              exact congrArg
   151	                (fun c => primeTauObservable (p := p) W c) hlabels

   153	/-- The prime-field exponent identity in `eq:pauli-product-power`, blueprint
   154	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:599-633`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1082-1089`. -/
   155	theorem primeTauObservable_pow {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   156	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]
   157	    [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (b : ZMod p) :
   158	    (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ b.val =
   159	      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => a i * algebraMap (ZMod p) K b) := by
   160	  rw [primeTauObservable_pow_nat]
   161	  congr 1
   162	  funext i
   163	  have hb : algebraMap (ZMod p) K b = (b.val : K) := by
   164	    rw [← map_natCast (algebraMap (ZMod p) K), ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
   165	  rw [nsmul_eq_mul, hb, mul_comm]

   167	/-- The characteristic-`p` consequence of `primeTauObservable_pow`, blueprint
   168	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:599-633`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1088-1089`. -/
   169	theorem primeTauObservable_pow_char {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   170	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]
   171	    [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) :
   172	    (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ p = 1 := by

   175	  have hlabel : (fun i => p • a i) = (0 : ι → K) := by

   180	/-- Taking the adjoint of a single-coordinate shift negates its label. -/
   181	private theorem star_primeTauShift {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   182	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (a : K) :
   183	    star (primeTauShift (p := p) a) = primeTauShift (p := p) (-a) := by
   184	  ext x y
   185	  by_cases h : y = x + a
   186	  · have h' : x = y + -a := by
   187	      rw [h]
   188	      abel
   189	    rw [Matrix.star_apply]
   190	    simp only [primeTauShift, if_pos h, if_pos h', star_one]
   191	  · have h' : x ≠ y + -a := by
   192	      intro h'
   193	      apply h
   194	      rw [h']
   195	      abel
   196	    rw [Matrix.star_apply]
   197	    simp only [primeTauShift, if_neg h, if_neg h', star_zero]

   201	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (b : K) :
   202	    star (primeTauPhase (p := p) b) = primeTauPhase (p := p) (-b) := by
   203	  ext x y
   204	  by_cases hxy : x = y
   205	  · subst y
   206	    simp only [Matrix.star_apply, primeTauPhase, if_pos]
   207	    rw [Complex.star_def]
   208	    simpa only [neg_mul] using
   209	      (AddChar.map_neg_eq_conj (ffChar (p := p) (F := K)) (b * x)).symm
   210	  · have hyx : y ≠ x := Ne.symm hxy
   211	    simp [Matrix.star_apply, primeTauPhase, hxy, hyx]

   302	/-- An additive character sends a finite sum to the product of its values. -/
   303	private theorem addChar_sum {A M ι : Type*} [AddCommMonoid A] [CommMonoid M]
   304	    [Fintype ι] (ψ : AddChar A M) (f : ι → A) :
   305	    ψ (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, ψ (f i) := by
   306	  classical
   307	  induction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) using Finset.induction_on with
   308	  | empty => simp
   309	  | @insert i s hi ih =>
   310	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hi, Finset.prod_insert hi, AddChar.map_add_eq_mul, ih]

   316	    [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] (a b : ι → K) :
   317	    primeTauObservable (p := p) true a * primeTauObservable (p := p) false b =
   318	      (ffChar (p := p) (F := K) (-dotProduct a b)) •
   319	        (primeTauObservable (p := p) false b * primeTauObservable (p := p) true a) := by
   320	  let ψ := ffChar (p := p) (F := K)
   321	  have hchar : ψ (-dotProduct a b) = ∏ i, ψ (-(a i) * b i) := by
   322	    calc
   323	      ψ (-dotProduct a b) = ψ (∑ i, -(a i) * b i) := by
   324	        congr 1
   325	        simp [dotProduct]
   326	      _ = ∏ i, ψ (-(a i) * b i) := addChar_sum ψ _
   327	  change productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a i)) *
   328	      productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (b i)) =
   329	    ψ (-dotProduct a b) •
   330	      (productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (b i)) *
   331	        productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a i)))
   332	  rw [productMatrix_mul, productMatrix_mul]
   333	  ext x y
   334	  simp only [productMatrix, primeTauShift_mul_primeTauPhase, Matrix.smul_apply,

     7	/-! # Pauli product, commutation, and cancellation identities
     8	
     9	The principal results are `lem:twisted-commutation` and `lem:cancellation` in
    10	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:553-660`, from
    11	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1056-1095,1124-1151`. The
    12	general-prime statements use the canonical character `ffChar`; binary
    13	declarations below are separately named QPBT specializations.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    17	
    18	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    19	
    20	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries MIPStarRE.Quantum
    21	
    22	/-- The shift observable in `lem:twisted-commutation`, blueprint
    23	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:553-597`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1056-1089`. -/
    24	noncomputable def primeTauShift {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    25	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    26	    (a : K) : Op K := fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    27	
    28	/-- The phase observable in `lem:twisted-commutation`, blueprint
    29	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:553-597`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1056-1089`. -/
    30	noncomputable def primeTauPhase {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    31	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    32	    (b : K) : Op K := fun i j =>
    33	  if i = j then ffChar (p := p) (F := K) (b * j) else 0
    34	
    35	/-- The multi-qudit observable in `lem:twisted-commutation`, with `false`
    36	denoting phase; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:553-597`, paper
    37	`04_preliminaries.tex:1073-1095,1141-1151`. -/
    38	noncomputable def primeTauObservable {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    39	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    40	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    41	  fun x y => ∏ i : ι, if W then primeTauShift (p := p) (a i) (x i) (y i)
    42	    else primeTauPhase (p := p) (a i) (x i) (y i)
    43	
    44	/-- The coordinatewise tensor-entry presentation used by the Pauli observables. -/
    45	private def productMatrix {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    46	    (A : ι → Matrix κ κ ℂ) : Matrix (ι → κ) (ι → κ) ℂ :=
    47	  fun x y => ∏ i, A i (x i) (y i)
    48	
    49	/-- Matrix multiplication distributes over `productMatrix`. -/
    50	private theorem productMatrix_mul {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    51	    [Fintype κ]
    52	    (A B : ι → Matrix κ κ ℂ) :
    53	    (productMatrix A * productMatrix B : Matrix (ι → κ) (ι → κ) ℂ) =
    54	      productMatrix (fun i => A i * B i) := by
    55	  classical
    56	  ext x y
    57	  simpa only [productMatrix, Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.prod_mul_distrib] using
    58	    (Fintype.prod_sum (fun i z => A i (x i) z * B i z (y i))).symm
    59	
    60	/-- Two single-coordinate shifts compose by adding their displacements. -/
    61	private theorem primeTauShift_mul {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    62	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (a a' : K) :
    63	    primeTauShift (p := p) a * primeTauShift (p := p) a' =
    64	      primeTauShift (p := p) (a + a') := by
    65	  ext x y
    66	  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, primeTauShift, add_comm, add_left_comm]
    67	
    68	/-- Two single-coordinate phases compose by adding their labels. -/
    69	private theorem primeTauPhase_mul {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    70	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (b b' : K) :
    71	    primeTauPhase (p := p) b * primeTauPhase (p := p) b' =
    72	      primeTauPhase (p := p) (b + b') := by
    73	  ext x y
    74	  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, primeTauPhase, add_mul, AddChar.map_add_eq_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The generalized Pauli observable with zero label is the identity. -/
    77	private theorem primeTauObservable_zero {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    78	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    79	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) :
    80	    primeTauObservable (p := p) W (0 : ι → K) = 1 := by
    81	  classical
    82	  ext x y
    83	  cases W <;>
    84	    simp only [primeTauObservable, if_true, Pi.zero_apply, primeTauShift,
    85	      primeTauPhase, zero_mul, AddChar.map_zero_eq_one, Matrix.one_apply]
    86	  all_goals
    87	    by_cases hxy : ∀ i, x i = y i
    88	    · have h : x = y := funext hxy
    89	      simp [h]
    90	    · simp only [not_forall] at hxy
    91	      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hxy
    92	      rw [Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ i) (by simp [hi])]
    93	      have h : x ≠ y := fun hxy => hi (congr_fun hxy i)
    94	      simp [h]

    96	/-- The product identity `eq:pauli-product-power`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:599-633`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1082-1089`. -/
    98	theorem primeTauObservable_mul {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    99	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]
   100	    [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a a' : ι → K) :
   101	    primeTauObservable (p := p) W a * primeTauObservable (p := p) W a' =
   102	      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (a + a') := by
   103	  cases W with
   104	  | false =>
   105	      change productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (a i)) *
   106	          productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (a' i)) =
   107	        productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) ((a + a') i))
   108	      simpa [primeTauPhase_mul] using
   109	        (productMatrix_mul
   110	          (A := fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (a i))
   111	          (B := fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (a' i)))
   112	  | true =>
   113	      change productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a i)) *
   114	          productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a' i)) =
   115	        productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) ((a + a') i))
   116	      simpa [primeTauShift_mul] using
   117	        (productMatrix_mul
   118	          (A := fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a i))
   119	          (B := fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a' i)))
   120	
   121	/-- Natural powers of a generalized Pauli observable multiply its label by
   122	repeated addition. -/
   123	private theorem primeTauObservable_pow_nat {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   124	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
   125	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (n : ℕ) :
   126	    (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n =
   127	      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) := by
   128	  induction n with
   129	  | zero =>
   130	      rw [pow_zero]
   131	      have hzero : (fun i => (0 : ℕ) • a i) = (0 : ι → K) := by
   132	        funext i
   133	        simp
   134	      rw [hzero]
   135	      exact (primeTauObservable_zero (p := p) (K := K) (ι := ι) W).symm
   136	  | succ n ih =>
   137	      calc
   138	        (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ (n + 1) =
   139	            (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n *
   140	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := pow_succ _ _
   141	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) *
   142	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := by rw [ih]
   143	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W ((fun i => n • a i) + a) :=
   144	              primeTauObservable_mul W _ _

   614	/-- A shift observable is the permutation matrix for addition by its label. -/
   615	private theorem tauObservable_X_apply
   616	    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
   617	    [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   618	    (a x y : ι → K) :

   629	    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
   630	    [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   631	    (a x y : ι → K) :

   637	  rw [Fintype.prod_ite_zero, prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct]

   642	/-- Binary-coordinate relabeling transports both generalized Pauli observables. -/
   643	private theorem tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
   644	    {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
   645	    (W : PauliKind) (a : Fin L → F.K) :
   646	    tauObservable W a =
   647	      Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   648	        (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   649	        (tauObservable W (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a)) := by
   650	  classical
   651	  ext x y
   652	  simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm]
   653	  cases W with
   654	  | X =>
   655	      rw [tauObservable_X_apply, tauObservable_X_apply]
   656	      have hadd := quditQubitLabelEquiv_add F L y a
   657	      rw [← hadd]
   658	      by_cases hshift : x = y + a
   659	      · rw [if_pos hshift, if_pos]
   660	        exact congrArg (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L) hshift
   661	      · rw [if_neg hshift, if_neg]
   662	        exact fun h => hshift ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
   663	  | Z =>
   664	      rw [tauObservable_Z_apply, tauObservable_Z_apply]
   665	      by_cases hxy : x = y
   666	      · subst y
   667	        rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl,
   668	          binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv,
   669	          quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L a,
   670	          quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L x]
   671	      · have hlabels : quditQubitLabelEquiv F L x ≠
   672	            quditQubitLabelEquiv F L y := fun h =>
   673	          hxy ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
   674	        rw [if_neg hxy, if_neg hlabels]

   676	/-- Fourier inversion transports the Pauli projectors along the binary label
   677	equivalence. -/
   678	private theorem pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
   679	    {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
   680	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K) :
   681	    pauliProj W u =
   682	      Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   683	        (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   684	        (pauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
   685	  classical
   686	  rw [pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable, pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable]
   687	  ext x y
   688	  simp only [Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
   689	    Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm]
   690	  rw [Fintype.card_congr (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L)]
   691	  congr 1
   692	  apply Fintype.sum_equiv (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L)
   693	  intro a
   694	  have hphase := congrArg phaseSign
   695	    (binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a u)
   696	  have hentry := congrFun
   697	    (congrFun (tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L W a) x) y
   698	  simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm] at hentry

   702	`pauliProj` to `ZMod 2`. This is the binary target in `lem:pauli-binary`,

   704	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
   705	noncomputable abbrev qubitPauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   706	    (W : PauliKind) (b : ι → ZMod 2) : Op (ι → ZMod 2) :=

   709	/-- `lem:pauli-binary`: the fixed binary coordinates induce an isometry that
   710	maps EPR states and generalized Pauli projectors to their qubit forms.
   711	Blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
   712	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`.

   714	**Local fix:** The source's final factor index is printed as
   715	`j ∈ {1, ..., q}`; the basis expansion at paper lines 1191--1194 shows that
   716	the intended range has `basisDim = log₂ q` entries. This correction is
   717	documented in `rem:pauli-binary-source` and issue #16. -/
   718	theorem exists_qubitIsometry (q : ℕ) (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) :
   719	    ∃ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L → F.K) ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   720	        EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2),
   721	      isometryTensor φ.toLinearIsometry φ.toLinearIsometry
   722	          (eprState (Fin L → F.K)) =
   723	          eprState (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2) ∧
   724	        ∀ (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K),
   725	          pauliProj W u =
   726	            conjIsometry φ.symm.toLinearIsometry
   727	              (qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
   728	  let e := quditQubitLabelEquiv F L
   729	  let φ := LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℂ ℂ e
   730	  refine ⟨φ, isometryTensor_piLpCongrLeft_epr e, ?_⟩
   731	  intro W u
   732	  rw [conjIsometry_piLpCongrLeft_symm]
   733	  exact pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L W u

1163	Since we only consider finite fields $\F_q$ such that $q = 2^k$ the maximally
  1164	entangled state $\ket{\EPR_q}$ and the corresponding qudit Pauli
  1165	observables/projectors are isomorphic to a tensor product of maximally entangled
  1166	states $\ket{\EPR_2}$ and \emph{qubit} Pauli observables/projectors
  1167	respectively; this is shown in the next lemma.
  1168	This is used to argue that the Pauli basis test (described in
  1169	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) gives a self-test for Pauli observables and
  1170	maximally entangled states over qubits.
  1171	
  1172	\begin{lemma}
  1173	  \label{lem:pauli-binary}
  1174	  For all admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ and integers $L$, there exists
  1175	  an isomorphism $\phi: (\C^q)^{\otimes L} \to (\C^2)^{\otimes L k}$
  1176	  such that\footnote{ Here we have applied the natural identifications between
  1177	  $(\C^q)^{\ot L} \ot (\C^q)^{\ot L}$ and $(\C^q \ot \C^q)^{\ot L}$,
  1178	  and between $(\C^2)^{\ot L k} \ot (C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ and $(\C^2 \ot
  1179	  \C^2)^{\ot Lk}$.}
  1180	\begin{equation}
  1181	    \label{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2}
  1182	    \phi \otimes \phi \, \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes L} =
  1183	    \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes L k}\;.
  1184	  \end{equation}
  1185	  Moreover, for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and for all $u \in \F_q^L$
  1186		\begin{equation}
  1187		\label{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}
  1188	  	\tau^W_u = \phi^\dagger\, \Bigl (\bigotimes_{i=1}^L
  1189	    \bigotimes_{j=1}^{k} \sigma^{W}_{u_{ij}} \Bigr) \, \phi\;.
  1190		\end{equation}
  1191		Here, the $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ denotes a vector of $\F_2$ values such that $u_i =
  1192	  \sum_j u_{ij} e_j$ for all $i \in \{1,\ldots,L\}$ with
  1193	  $\{e_1,\ldots,e_{k}\}$ being the self-dual normal basis of $\F_q$ over $\F_2$
  1194	  specified by Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_basis}.
  1195	  For $i\in\{1,\ldots,L\}$ and $j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$ the $(i,j)$-th factor
  1196	  $\sigma^{W}_{u_{ij}}$ denotes the projector $\frac{1}{2} \left ( \Id +
  1197	    (-1)^{u_{ij}} \sigma^W(1) \right)$ acting on the $s$-th qubit of
  1198	  $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes L k}$, where $s = (i-1) k + j$.
  1199	\end{lemma}
  1200	
  1201	\begin{proof}
  1202	Define the isometry $\theta : \C^q \to (\C^2)^{\otimes k}$ as $\theta\,
  1203	  \ket{a} = \ket{a_1} \otimes \ket{ a_2} \cdots \ket{a_k}$ where $\kappa(a) = (a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k)
  1204	  \in \F_2^k$ is the bijection introduced in Section~\ref{sec:finite-fields}
  1205	  corresponding to the basis $\{e_1,\ldots,e_k\}$. Observe that
  1206	  $\theta \otimes \theta \ket{\EPR_{2^k}} = \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot k}$.
  1207	
  1208	  Let $a \in \F_q$, and let $\kappa(a) = (a_1,\ldots,a_k) \in \F_2^k$.
  1209	  Then from~\eqref{eq:pauli-inversion-0}, we get
  1210	  \begin{equation}
  1211	    \label{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli-1}
  1212	    \begin{split}
  1213	      \tau^W_a
  1214	      & = \E_{b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(a b)} \, \tau^W(b) \\
  1215	      & = \E_{b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(\sum_j a_j e_j b)} \, \tau^W(b) \\
  1216	      & = \E_{b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\sum_j a_j b_j} \,
  1217	      \tau^W \left ( \sum_j b_j e_j \right) \;,
  1218	    \end{split}
  1219	  \end{equation}
  1220	  where $b = \sum_j b_j e_j$; since the basis $\{e_j \}$ is self-dual, we have
  1221	  that $b_j = \tr(b e_j)$. From~\eqref{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli-1} and
  1222	  the product relation in~\eqref{eq:pauli-product-power} we get that
  1223	  \begin{equation}
  1224			\label{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli}
  1225	    \begin{split}
  1226	      \tau^W_a & = \E_{b_1,\, \ldots,\, b_k \in \F_2}\,
  1227	      \prod_{j=1}^k (-1)^{a_j b_j} \, \tau^W(b_j e_j) \\
  1228	      & = \prod_{j=1}^k \E_{b_j \in \F_2} (-1)^{a_j b_j} \, \tau^W(b_j e_j)\;,
  1229	    \end{split}
  1230	  \end{equation}
  1231	  where we have the used the fact that the expectation is over iid
  1232	  $b_1, \dots, b_k$ to take it inside the product in the second line.
  1233	  Next we claim that for all $c \in \F_2$, we have $\tau^W(c e_j) =
  1234	  \theta^\dagger \sigma^{W,j} (c) \theta$ where $\sigma^{W,j}(c) = \Id$ if $c =
  1235	  0$, and otherwise is the Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $j$-th qubit of
  1236	  $(\C^2)^{\otimes k}$. This can be verified by comparing the actions of both
  1237	  operators on the basis states of $\C^q$.
  1238	  
  1239	  Thus we obtain that the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli} is
  1240	  equal to
  1241	  \begin{align}
  1242			\prod_{j=1}^k \E_{b_j \in \F_2} (-1)^{a_j b_j} \,
  1243	    \Big [ \theta^\dagger \sigma^{W,j}(b_j) \theta \Big ]
  1244	    & = \theta^\dagger \, \bigotimes_{j=1}^k
  1245	      \Big ( \E_{b_j \in \F_2} (-1)^{a_j b_j} \, \sigma^{W}(b_j) \Big) \theta \\
  1246			& = \theta^\dagger \Big (\bigotimes_{j=1}^k \sigma^W_{b_j} \Big) \theta.
  1247			\label{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli-2}
  1248	  \end{align}
  1249	  Define $\phi = \theta^{\otimes L}$. It is evident
  1250	  that~\eqref{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2} holds for this choice of $\phi$, and
  1251	  it remains to show~\eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}. The projector $\tau^W_u$ can be
  1252	  decomposed as the tensor product $\bigotimes_{i=1}^L \tau^{W}_{u_i}$
  1253	  where $\tau^{W}_{u_i}$ acts on the $i$-th factor of $(\C^q)^{\otimes L}$.
  1254	  Express each $u_i$ as $\sum_j u_{ij} e_j$ where $u_{ij} \in \F_2$. Then from
  1255	  Equation~\eqref{eq:qudit-to-qubit-pauli-2} we get that
  1256	  \begin{equation}
  1257	  	\tau^W_u = \bigotimes_{i=1}^L \tau^W_{u_i}
  1258	    = \phi^\dagger \left( \bigotimes_{i=1}^L
  1259	      \bigotimes_{j=1}^k \sigma^W_{u_{ij}} \right) \phi,
  1260	  \end{equation}
  1261	  which establishes Equation~\eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}. 
  1262	\end{proof}
  1263

743	\begin{proof}
   744		\uses{lem:pauli-observable-expansion, lem:downsize_field,
   745			lem:twisted-commutation}
   746		Define the isometry $\theta : \C^q \to (\C^2)^{\ot k}$ by
   747		$\theta\ket{a} = \ket{a_1} \ot \dots \ot \ket{a_k}$, where
   748		$\kappa(a) = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is the binary representation with respect
   749		to the fixed basis; since $\kappa$ is a bijection, $\theta$ is a unitary
   750		and $\theta \ot \theta\, \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_{2^k}} =
   751		\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot k}$. For $a \in \F_q$ with
   752		$\kappa(a) = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$, the inversion formula of
   753		Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion} gives
   754		$\tau^W_a = \E_{b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ab)}\, \tau^W(b)$; writing
   755		$b = \sum_j b_j e_j$, self-duality of the basis gives
   756		$b_j = \tr(b e_j)$ (item 1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field}) and hence
   757		$\tr(ab) = \sum_j a_j b_j$. The product relation of
   758		Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation} factors
   759		$\tau^W(b) = \prod_j \tau^W(b_j e_j)$, so the expectation factors over
   760		independent $b_1, \dots, b_k \in \F_2$. A computation on basis states shows
   761		that for all $c \in \F_2$, $\tau^W(c e_j) = \theta^\dagger\,
   762		\sigma^{W,j}(c)\, \theta$, where $\sigma^{W,j}(c)$ is the identity for
   763		$c = 0$ and the Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $j$-th qubit of
   764		$(\C^2)^{\ot k}$ for $c = 1$. Averaging,
   765		$\E_{b_j \in \F_2} (-1)^{a_j b_j} \sigma^W(b_j) =
   766		\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\Id + (-1)^{a_j}\sigma^W(1)\bigr) = \sigma^W_{a_j}$,
   767		whence $\tau^W_a = \theta^\dagger \bigl(\bigotimes_j
   768		\sigma^W_{a_j}\bigr) \theta$. Taking $\phi = \theta^{\ot L}$ and tensoring
   769		the last identity over the $L$ qudits, using
   770		$\tau^W_u = \bigotimes_{i=1}^L \tau^W_{u_i}$, yields both displayed
   771		identities.
   772	\end{proof}

   774	\begin{remark}\label{rem:pauli-binary-source}
   775		In the source statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary} in
   776		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, the index range of the qubit factor is printed as
   777		$j \in \{1, \dots, q\}$; the intended range, used above, is
   778		$j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, as the $i$-th qudit is mapped to $k$ qubits. The
   779		source also quantifies over arbitrary integers $L$; the statement above
   780		takes $L$ to be a natural number, including zero, and uses the usual
   781		empty-product convention for the tensor powers when $L=0$.
   782	\end{remark}

    48	/-- In characteristic two, the standard additive character is the sign

    51	    phaseSign t = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) t := by
    52	  by_cases ht : t = 0
    53	  · subst t
    54	    rw [phaseSign, if_pos rfl]
    55	    exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_zero_eq_one.symm

    57	      have hval_ne : t.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_ne_zero t).mpr ht

    59	      omega
    60	    have ht_one : t = 1 := (ZMod.val_eq_one (by omega) t).mp hval

    62	    rw [phaseSign, if_neg one_ne_zero]
    63	    change (-1 : ℂ) = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod 2)

     Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single (e y)]
   · rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single (e x)]
     · simp [piLpCongrLeft_matrix_apply]
     · intro j hj
       have hxj : x ≠ e.symm j := by
         intro h
         apply hj
         simp [h]
       simp [piLpCongrLeft_matrix_apply, hxj]
   · intro i hi
     have hyi : y ≠ e.symm i := by
       intro h
       apply hi
       simp [h]
     simp [piLpCongrLeft_matrix_apply, hyi]
 
 /-- The label equivalence obtained by expanding each field element in the fixed
 self-dual binary basis. -/
 private noncomputable def quditQubitLabelEquiv {q : ℕ}
     (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) :
     (Fin L → F.K) ≃ (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2) :=
   (Equiv.piCongrRight (fun _ : Fin L => F.binaryCoordinates.toEquiv)).trans
     (Equiv.curry (Fin L) (Fin F.basisDim) (ZMod 2)).symm
 
 /-- The label equivalence is the uncurried form of `kappaVec`. -/
 private theorem quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec {q : ℕ}
     (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) (u : Fin L → F.K) :
     quditQubitLabelEquiv F L u = kappaVec F u := by
   rfl
 
 /-- Self-duality identifies the field trace pairing with the binary coordinate
 pairing after relabeling. -/
 private theorem binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv
     {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) (a u : Fin L → F.K) :
     binTrace F.K (dotProduct a u) =
       binTrace (ZMod 2)
         (dotProduct (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a) (kappaVec F u)) := by
   simp only [dotProduct, map_sum, binTrace_mul_eq_dotProduct F,
     Algebra.trace_self_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, quditQubitLabelEquiv,
     Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.curry_symm_apply, kappaVec, basisCoordVec]
   rfl
 
-/-- The binary sign character sends sums to products. -/
-private theorem phaseSign_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ZMod 2) :
-    phaseSign (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, phaseSign (f i) := by
-  simpa only [phaseSign_eq_stdAddChar] using
-    (addChar_sum (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)) f)
-
-/-- The product of the coordinate phases is the phase of the trace pairing. -/
-private theorem prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct
-    {K ι : Type*} [CommRing K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι]
-    (a u : ι → K) :
-    (∏ i, phaseSign (binTrace K (a i * u i))) =
-      phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a u)) := by
-  rw [← phaseSign_sum]
-  simp [dotProduct]
-
 /-- The coordinate label equivalence preserves addition. -/
 private theorem quditQubitLabelEquiv_add {q : ℕ}
     (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) (a b : Fin L → F.K) :
     quditQubitLabelEquiv F L (a + b) =
       quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a + quditQubitLabelEquiv F L b := by
   ext p
   rcases p with ⟨i, j⟩
   change F.binaryCoordinates (a i + b i) j =
     F.binaryCoordinates (a i) j + F.binaryCoordinates (b i) j
   simp
 
 /-- A shift observable is the permutation matrix for addition by its label. -/
 private theorem tauObservable_X_apply
     {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
     [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
     (a x y : ι → K) :
     tauObservable .X a x y = if x = y + a then 1 else 0 := by
   change (∏ i : ι, if x i = y i + a i then 1 else 0) = _
   rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
   have hsupport : (∀ i, x i = y i + a i) ↔ x = y + a := by
     simpa only [Pi.add_apply] using
       (funext_iff (f := x) (g := y + a)).symm
   simp only [hsupport]
 
 /-- A phase observable is diagonal, with its phase given by the trace pairing. -/
 private theorem tauObservable_Z_apply
     {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
     [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
     (a x y : ι → K) :
     tauObservable .Z a x y =
       if x = y then phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a y)) else 0 := by
   change
     (∏ i : ι,
       if x i = y i then phaseSign (binTrace K (a i * y i)) else 0) = _
   rw [Fintype.prod_ite_zero, prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct]
   have hsupport : (∀ i, x i = y i) ↔ x = y :=
     (funext_iff (f := x) (g := y)).symm
   simp only [hsupport]
 
 /-- Binary-coordinate relabeling transports both generalized Pauli observables. -/
 private theorem tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
     {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
     (W : PauliKind) (a : Fin L → F.K) :
     tauObservable W a =
       Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
         (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
         (tauObservable W (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a)) := by
   classical
   ext x y
   simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm]
   cases W with
   | X =>
       rw [tauObservable_X_apply, tauObservable_X_apply]
       have hadd := quditQubitLabelEquiv_add F L y a
       rw [← hadd]
       by_cases hshift : x = y + a
       · rw [if_pos hshift, if_pos]
         exact congrArg (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L) hshift
       · rw [if_neg hshift, if_neg]
         exact fun h => hshift ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
   | Z =>
       rw [tauObservable_Z_apply, tauObservable_Z_apply]
       by_cases hxy : x = y
       · subst y
         rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl,
           binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv,
           quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L a,
           quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L x]
       · have hlabels : quditQubitLabelEquiv F L x ≠
             quditQubitLabelEquiv F L y := fun h =>
           hxy ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
         rw [if_neg hxy, if_neg hlabels]
 
 /-- Fourier inversion transports the Pauli projectors along the binary label
 equivalence. -/
 private theorem pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
     {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
     (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K) :
     pauliProj W u =
       Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
